Fracking chemicals contaminated drinking water in Pennsylvania, study finds

The specific 'fracking chemical' they seized on is 2-Butoxyethanol, which the concentration of in the one household sample they could detect it in was in the ppt (parts per trillion).

It sounds really scary, this 'fracking chemical'. So doing some looking around you find out that this is something with a permissible level of 50 ppm (parts per million) in food and beverages, that it's in a lot of common household items, and that the FDA considers it a safe additive even at several orders of magnitude higher than detected in the sample. It's a surfactant and anti-microbial, and there's no way to prove that the amount detected in that sample actually came from fracking at all.

In other words, an infinitesimal amount of soap was found in water that came out of a kitchen faucet. Color me shocked.

Fracking (READ: unconventional oil and gas development) is not healthy for children and other living things, period. That the health and safety issues with fracking are more recently being reported on in scientific papers is due to the enormous power of the petroleum lobby and Halliburton exemption. Defending the practice as "safe" is over, even the USGS reports that fracking (that is, the waste injection that is a by-product of fracking) causes earthquakes. If anyone posts some dumb comment about how these are only "minor" tremors, they are woefully uninformed.

Those who argue about a drop of soap in a kitchen faucet are ignoring the demonstrable negative effects of this process on water and air quality. Make whatever clarifying points about this particular study or compound that seem to make you feel better about what you are drinking but defending the process based on criticism of one study? Yes, I do live at ground zero for fracking. It's an ugly process that has crapped on our air quality here. Every week there are many surface spills reported in this area, which have adversely impacted surface waters in the area also. We have had earthquakes as well. This is the truth of unconventional oil and gas development, not that there's a drop of surfactant in your water - oh my.
